All 22 'revert with mem[_N len 4], ...' now show the selector and decoded payload, e.g. 'revert with 0x4ff9e48a, 32, _24, mem[_23 + 68 len _24], ...' (unknown88ea09ee 248, 270; unknown94bbb012; updateNodes). A call whose function printed as 'mem[_2070 len 4]' is now unknownfba64a7c(?).

regressions.source: CapabilitiesRegistry.getNode: s_capabilities[hashedCapabilityIds[i]] strings, s_nodes[p2pId].capabilitiesPerDon; getDONs-type view reading s_capabilityConfigurationContracts (slot 3)
regressions.issue: A mapping slot computed in the scratch words (mem[0], mem[32]) is no longer resolved once a store at a free-pointer-relative address follows it: the hash is printed as sha3(mem[0 len 64]) / mem[32] at its later uses. The slot the old text named (stor3[...].field_256, sha3(node, 18) + 6) becomes opaque. The memory-dependent hash is also printed after stores the text does not prove disjoint from [0, 64).
regressions.rule: Bind a keccak of scratch memory to a value at the point where it is computed. Use the free pointer's constant floor (>= 0x80) to prove that stores at mem[64] + k (k >= 0) never reach [0, 0x40], so the scratch contents stay known.

regressions.source: copies of storage strings into memory (string memory s = s_capabilities[...].labelledName / DON names)
regressions.issue: Four storage-to-memory string copies that round 1 showed as copy lines are while loops again. The copy base, held in a variable before (_342 = mem[64]), is now re-read as mem[64] inside the loop, which writes memory, so the copy is no longer proven (in getNode the source also depends on mem[0]). Storage copy lines 69 -> 65, whiles 112 -> 116.
regressions.rule: Evaluate the copy base once, before the loop (a load of slot 0x40 is a value, not a location). Use the pointer floor to prove that the loop's stores at base + i never hit slot 0x40 or the scratch words, then fold the loop into 'mem[base len n] = stor[s len k]'.

regressions.issue: Slot variables used several times are now inlined at each use as long hash expressions, some built from memory slices. Lines that read stor[_92 + 5] or stor[_5] become 150-250 characters; mem[0] does resolve now in some of them.
regressions.rule: Keep a named temporary for a hashed slot that is used more than once (substitute only short expressions).

improvements: Old finding 2 is fixed (22 custom-error reverts decoded); a call named 'mem[_2070 len 4]' now shows its selector. supportsInterface is named and its argument decoded. P4 keys (stor19[concat(mem[0])], stor14[concat(mem[0])], stor9[concat(mem[0])]) now use values. Logs decoded (Array(len, data), constant 0 payloads), and several returns are split into offset/length/data words. Hex constants show whole bytes (0x01ffc9a7...).
notes: Diff (1,575 lines) read hunk by hunk with per-function diffs (22 changed). The changed functions' text grew 2% in characters (lines over 240 chars 128 -> 139). Regressions 1-3 share one cause: values read from mem[64] (or from the scratch words) are now re-read at their uses after stores at free-pointer-relative addresses, instead of being kept as values. The selector-as-memory-slice display ('target.mem[a len 4]') already existed in round 1 here. The P4/P7/P8 counts are estimates.
summary: Custom-error reverts and several keys and logs are now decoded (old finding 2 fixed), but four storage-string copies fell back to while loops, getNode's mapping slots and one call target became opaque scratch-memory hashes, two returns went back to raw memory, and inlined slot expressions lengthen many lines.
